panel.summary: MemNoteStore keeps an unbounded stack of full-text snapshots and replaces the whole document on undo
panel.evidence: `pushUndo` (memory.ts, `private pushUndo`) appends a full copy of the note text on every un-batched `editText` and every mutating `batch`, with no cap and no eviction — one whole-document string per keystroke, retained for the life of the store. The class comment justifies it as "cheap enough for a note", which is only true for short sessions. Separately, `undo()`/`redo()` emit `{ type: 'replace', content }`, which `note-sync.applyRemote` turns into a `from: 0, to: doc.length` replacement of the entire document — that discards CodeMirror's per-change mapping (selection/scroll land wherever a whole-doc replace maps them) where the Yorkie store emits precise `edits`. Impact is bounded today because MemNoteStore is only referenced from tests and the package export surface (grep: only editor.test.ts, note-sync.test.ts, memory.test.ts, index.ts, node.ts).
panel.finding_key: packages/notes/src/store/memory.ts::memnotestore keeps an unbounded stack of full-text snapshots and replaces the whole document on undo

coderabbit.detail: **Consider capping the snapshot history.** `undoStack` stores one full-text snapshot per un-batched edit and never drops old entries. A long editing session in a large note keeps every historical version in memory. A fixed cap keeps memory bounded and matches typical editor behavior.
